topics.title: Introduction and Scope of AS 13
explain: AS 13 deals with accounting for investments in financial statements and disclosures.
It does not cover interest, dividends, and rentals covered by AS 9.
It excludes operating or finance leases and retirement benefit plans.
It excludes mutual funds, venture capital funds, banks, and public financial institutions.
Stock-in-trade is not an investment, but current investment valuation rules apply to it.

flow.title: Scope Applicability Check
steps: Check if asset is held as investment
Verify asset is not stock-in-trade
Ensure entity is not bank or mutual fund
Apply AS 13 rules for valuation

topics.example: A manufacturing company buying government bonds follows AS 13, but a bank holding bonds for trading follows banking statutes.
remember: Stock-in-trade is excluded from definition but follows current investment valuation rules.
mistakes: Applying AS 13 to bank treasury portfolios or mutual fund investments.

quiz.q: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of AS 13?
quiz.why: AS 13 specifically excludes mutual funds, banks, and venture capital funds.

quiz.q: How is stock-in-trade of shares treated under AS 13?
o: Fully governed as an AS 13 investment
Not an investment, but uses current investment valuation rules
quiz.why: Stock-in-trade is not an investment by definition, but current investment rules apply with modifications.

topics.title: Key Definitions in AS 13
explain: Investments are assets held for earning income like dividends, interest, or rentals, or for capital appreciation.
Assets held as stock-in-trade (inventory) are not investments.
Fair Value is the amount for which an asset could be exchanged between knowledgeable, willing parties in an arm's length deal.
Market Value is the amount obtainable from selling an investment in an open market, net of disposal expenses.

flow.title: Determining Asset Classification
steps: Identify purpose of holding asset
If held for sale in business, classify as Inventory
If held for interest, dividend, or growth, classify as Investment

topics.example: If a builder holds flats for sale, it is inventory; if a trader buys flats to earn rental income, it is an investment.
remember: Market value is net of selling expenses, whereas fair value is an arm's length exchange price.
mistakes: Confusing stock-in-trade held for regular trading with short-term investments.

quiz.q: What is Fair Value as per AS 13?
o: Arm's length exchange price between willing parties
Highest price offered in a auction
Book value reported in balance sheet
quiz.why: Fair value is the exchange price between knowledgeable, willing parties in an arm's length transaction.

quiz.q: Market value of an investment is calculated as:
o: Open market sale price net of disposal expenses
quiz.why: Market value is the net amount obtainable from open market sale after deducting selling expenses.

topics.title: Classification of Investments
explain: Investments are classified into Current Investments and Long-term Investments.
A Current Investment is readily realisable and intended to be held for not more than one year.
Intention to hold for less than one year is judged at the time of purchase.
A Long-term Investment is an investment other than a current investment.
Sub-classifications include Govt/Trust securities, Shares/bonds, Investment properties, and Others.

flow.title: Investment Classification Process
steps: Purchase investment asset
Check if readily realisable
Check intention at purchase date (<= 1 year)
Classify as Current if both true
Classify as Long-term if held > 1 year

topics.example: Company A buys shares on 1st April intending to sell within 6 months. It is classified as a current investment regardless of market volatility.
remember: Intention to hold is judged at the purchase date, not at the balance sheet date.
mistakes: Classifying a readily marketable long-term holding as a current investment just because it can be sold anytime.

quiz.q: When is the intention to hold an investment judged for classification?
o: At the end of the financial year
At the time of purchase of investment
quiz.why: The intention to hold for not more than one year is judged right at the time of purchase.

quiz.q: What is a long-term investment under AS 13?
o: An investment other than a current investment
An investment held for exactly 3 years
quiz.why: AS 13 defines a long-term investment simply as an investment other than a current investment.

topics.title: Cost of Investments
explain: Initial cost includes purchase price plus direct charges like brokerage, fees, and duties.
If acquired by issuing shares, cost is the fair value of securities issued.
If acquired in asset exchange, cost is fair value of asset given up or acquired (whichever is clearer).
Pre-acquisition interest or dividend received is deducted from the investment cost.
Cost of subscribed right shares is added to the carrying amount of original holding.
Sale proceeds of un-subscribed right entitlements are credited to Profit and Loss statement.

flow.title: Computing Initial Cost
steps: Take basic purchase price
Add brokerage, fees, and duties
Deduct pre-acquisition interest/dividend received
Arrive at initial carrying cost

topics.example: Bought deposit worth Rs 200 lakhs paying Rs 1 lakh brokerage. Total initial cost credited to investment account is Rs 201 lakhs.
remember: Sale of right entitlement goes to P&L unless bought cum-right and ex-right market price dropped below cost.
mistakes: Crediting pre-acquisition dividend income to P&L instead of reducing investment cost.

quiz.q: How are brokerage and duty charges treated upon purchase of investment?
o: Added to the cost of investment
quiz.why: Acquisition charges like brokerage, duties, and fees form part of the cost of investment.

quiz.q: What happens to sale proceeds of right entitlement when rights are not subscribed?
o: Deducted from cost of original shares
quiz.why: Sale proceeds of rights sold in the market are credited directly to the P&L statement.

topics.title: Carrying Amount and Valuation of Investments
explain: Current investments are carried at lower of cost and fair value.
Valuation of current investments must be done individually or category-wise, not on global basis.
Reduction to fair value for current investments is debited to P&L.
Subsequent increase in current investment value up to original cost is credited to P&L.
Long-term investments are carried at cost.
Reduction in long-term investments is made only for decline that is 'other than temporary'.

flow.title: Valuation Logic at Balance Sheet Date
steps: Check investment category
If Current: compare Cost vs Fair Value individually
Record Current at Lower of Cost or Fair Value
If Long-term: carry at Cost
If Long-term has permanent drop: write down to P&L

topics.example: A current share bought for Rs 100 has market value Rs 80 on March 31. It is valued at Rs 80 and Rs 20 loss is debited to P&L.
remember: Global valuation of current investments is not allowed; carry individually for prudence.
mistakes: Writing down a long-term investment for temporary market fluctuations.

quiz.q: Current investments are carried in financial statements at:
o: Lower of cost and fair value
Higher of cost and fair value
quiz.why: AS 13 mandates carrying current investments at the lower of cost and fair value.

quiz.q: When is the carrying amount of a long-term investment reduced?
o: Whenever market value falls below cost
On a global portfolio valuation basis
When decline in value is other than temporary
quiz.why: Long-term investments are reduced only when there is a decline other than temporary.

topics.title: Investment Properties
explain: An Investment Property is an investment in land or buildings not occupied for business use.
It is accounted for using the cost model as prescribed in AS 10 (Revised).
Cost of shares in co-operative society granting right to hold property is added to property cost.
Rental income earned from investment property is recognized as income under AS 9.

flow.title: Investment Property Accounting
steps: Identify land/building asset
Check business use (if none, it is Investment Property)
Measure cost including society share cost
Apply AS 10 cost model (Cost less depreciation)

topics.example: A company buys a commercial building solely to earn rent. It is classified as an investment property and depreciated per AS 10 rules.
remember: Investment properties follow the cost model under AS 10, not fair value revaluations under AS 13.
mistakes: Valuing investment properties at lower of cost and market value like current investments.

quiz.q: Investment properties are accounted for under which standard's cost model?
quiz.why: AS 13 requires investment properties to be accounted for under the cost model of AS 10 (Revised).

o: Land or building not occupied for operational use
Office building owned and used by directors
quiz.why: Investment property is land or building not intended to be occupied substantially for enterprise use.

topics.title: Disposal of Investments
explain: Difference between net disposal proceeds and carrying amount is recognized in P&L.
Disposal proceeds are net of expenses like brokerage and transfer fees.
When selling a portion of an investment holding, cost is calculated using weighted average cost method.

flow.title: Calculating Profit/Loss on Disposal
steps: Calculate Gross Selling Price
Deduct selling costs (brokerage)
Determine Average Carrying Amount of sold portion
Gain/Loss = Net Proceeds - Average Carrying Amount
Transfer Net Gain/Loss to P&L

topics.example: Selling 500 shares out of 1,000 shares requires allocating 50% of total carrying cost as the cost of sold shares.
remember: Always use average carrying amount when disposing part of a holding.
mistakes: Using FIFO or LIFO for investment disposals when average cost is specified by standard.

quiz.q: How is cost calculated when disposing of a part of investment holding?
o: On the basis of average carrying amount of total holding
quiz.why: AS 13 mandates allocating carrying amount based on the average carrying amount of total holding.

quiz.q: Where is the profit or loss on disposal of investments recognized?
quiz.why: The difference between carrying amount and net disposal proceeds is credited or debited to P&L.

topics.title: Reclassification of Investments
explain: Investments may be reclassified between long-term and current categories.
Reclassification from Long-term to Current: transferred at lower of cost and carrying amount.
Reclassification from Current to Long-term: transferred at lower of cost and fair value.
Transfers take effect on the date of reclassification.

flow.title: Reclassification Transfer Rules
steps: Identify transfer direction
If Long-term -> Current: measure at lower of Cost & Carrying Amount
If Current -> Long-term: measure at lower of Cost & Fair Value
Record transfer entry at determined value

topics.example: Reclassifying current investment costing Rs 15 lakhs with fair value Rs 6.5 lakhs to long-term: transfer at Rs 6.5 lakhs and charge Rs 8.5 lakhs loss to P&L.
remember: Long-term to Current = Lower of Cost and Carrying Amount; Current to Long-term = Lower of Cost and Fair Value.
mistakes: Transferring current investments to long-term at market value when market value exceeds cost.

quiz.q: When long-term investments are reclassified as current investments, transfer is made at:
o: Lower of cost and carrying amount
quiz.why: Transfers from long-term to current are made at the lower of cost and carrying amount at transfer date.

quiz.q: Transfer of investments from Current to Long-term is made at:
o: Lower of cost and fair value at transfer date
quiz.why: Reclassification from current to long-term is done at the lower of cost and fair value on transfer date.

topics.title: Disclosure Requirements
explain: Disclose accounting policies for determining carrying amounts of investments.
Disclose amounts in P&L for interest, dividends, and rentals (split by current and long-term).
Disclose profits and losses on disposal and changes in carrying amounts.
Disclose significant restrictions on ownership, realisability, or remittance of proceeds.
Disclose aggregate amounts of quoted and unquoted investments and market value of quoted ones.
Disclose classification of investments into current and long-term.

flow.title: Financial Statement Disclosure Checklist
steps: State accounting policies used
Classify into Current and Long-term
Show P&L income and disposal gains/losses
List aggregate quoted/unquoted amounts and market values
Report ownership/remittance restrictions

topics.example: Footnotes in balance sheet must explicitly state total quoted investments (with market value) and total unquoted investments.
remember: Dividends from subsidiary companies must be shown separately in P&L disclosure.
mistakes: Forgetting to disclose the aggregate market value of quoted investments.

quiz.q: Which of the following disclosures is required by AS 13?
o: Aggregate market value of quoted investments
quiz.why: AS 13 requires disclosing aggregate amounts of quoted investments along with their aggregate market value.

quiz.q: How should gross investment income be disclosed in P&L?
o: Net of advance tax paid only
Separately showing income from long-term and current investments
As a direct addition to capital reserve
quiz.why: AS 13 mandates showing interest, dividends, and rentals separately for long-term and current investments.
